 Operations Supervisor, Distribution Center
 About the Role
 The Operations Supervisor provides hands-on leadership for the day-to-day operations of a distribution center team, with a primary focus on receiving and inbound operations. You will lead employees to safely and accurately receive, inspect, stage, and move healthcare products while meeting expectations for quality, service, productivity, and cost.
 This role plans daily work, assigns labour, monitors operational KPIs, coaches employees, and resolves issues that could affect product flow or customer service. You will also partner with other supervisors and departments to support efficient operations across receiving, inventory, outbound, narcotics, and other warehouse functions.
 What You’ll Do
 Lead, coach, and supervise employees to achieve safety, quality, service, productivity, and cost expectations.
 Plan daily warehouse activities, assign labour, and adjust resources based on inbound volume and operational priorities.
 Oversee receiving operations, including unloading, inspection, staging, receiving accuracy, product integrity, and inbound workflow.
 Ensure products are promptly moved to appropriate temperature-controlled, restricted, or designated storage areas.
 Monitor operational KPIs and employee performance, identify barriers, and take action to improve results.
 Coach and develop employees, recognize performance, and address performance concerns as appropriate.
 Ensure team members are properly trained and follow standard operating procedures, quality requirements, and safe work practices.
 Investigate and escalate receiving discrepancies, product damage, temperature concerns, and other operational risks.
 Coordinate importation requirements, product releases, receiving documentation, and related operational reporting.
 Partner with other supervisors and cross-functional teams to maintain efficient site-wide product flow.
 Support recruitment, onboarding, training, and development of new employees.
 Identify and support continuous improvement opportunities that strengthen safety, quality, productivity, and service.
 Serve as Site Security Officer and support site security requirements, controls, and follow-up.
 Serve as Health and Safety Lead, supporting inspections, investigations, corrective actions, and employee safety awareness.
 Act as Quality Person in Charge (QPIC) and/or Alternate Quality Person in Charge (AQPIC), as applicable, and support compliance with applicable Canadian requirements for controlled substances.
 Maintain the security of narcotics vaults, cages, and other controlled-access areas.
 Basic Requirements
 3+ years of relevant distribution center, warehouse, receiving, logistics, or related operational experience, including demonstrated leadership capabilities. 
 Preferred Skills/Experience
 Previous experience leading or supervising employees in a distribution center, warehouse, manufacturing, or logistics environment.
 Experience with receiving, shipping, inventory control, material handling, or warehouse operations .
 Experience working in a regulated, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or quality-controlled distribution environment.
 Experience monitoring warehouse KPIs , productivity, accuracy, quality, and service metrics.
 Experience with warehouse management systems, inventory systems, computers, and warehouse automation.
 Forklift, reach truck, order picker, or other powered industrial equipment experience.
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality and process compliance.
 Strong coaching, communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
 Ability to adapt priorities based on changing volume and operational requirements.
 Experience identifying or implementing continuous improvement opportunities.
 Experience supporting workplace health and safety programs.
 Familiarity with controlled substances, regulated products, site security, or QPIC/AQPIC responsibilities is an asset.
 In-Office / Physical Requirements
 This is an on-site distribution center position .
 Must be able to work the assigned shift and adjust hours when operational needs require.
 Regularly works in an active warehouse environment and may spend extended periods standing or walking.
 Must be able to bend, reach, stretch, carry, and perform other physical activities required in a distribution environment.
 Must be able to lift and move up to 40 lbs. independently , with heavier items handled through team-lifting practices.
 A clear CPIC check may be required based on position and site requirements.

 Work with Global Analytics, Product and Marketing Operations to put propensity scores, next-best-action logic and automated insights into live journeys.
 Optimization 
 Maintain lifecycle dashboards and reporting tied to engagement, adoption, retention, expansion and revenue.
 Run the test-and-learn roadmap across journey design, messaging, segmentation, channel mix, timing, personalization and offers.
 Analyze campaign and journey performance and act on opportunities to optimize and scale.

 2+ years of experience managing people or leading lifecycle, CRM or marketing automation programs.

 Advanced, hands-on proficiency in Marketo or a similar platform.
 Experience building complex automated journeys using behavioral triggers, customer attributes, lifecycle stages, scoring, suppression logic and dynamic content.
 Solid understanding of customer lifecycle management, retention, adoption, engagement, renewal support and expansion motions.
 Experience using data to build audiences, measure performance and optimize campaigns.

 Experience applying AI, predictive analytics, personalization or experimentation in marketing programs.

 Bachelor's degree in marketing, business, analytics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 
 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
 Instacart is a Flex First team 
 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 
 Overview
 Instacart's Enterprise Solutions team partners with Global grocery and retail chains to power their digital commerce through StorefrontPro, Enterprise API (Fulfillment and Ads), CarrotAds, and adjacent Enterprise Solutions products. We're seeking a Director, Customer Success to lead the Customer Success organization — accountable for post-live value realization across the enterprise software portfolio.
 In this highly visible role, you will lead senior managers and Customer Success Managers who serve as the strategic advisor of Instacart to retailer executives. You'll own retailer value realization, measured through adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score coverage, at-risk portfolio management, CSAT, and QBR quality across the portfolio. You'll partner closely with Business Development, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness. You'll also partner with Enterprise Solutions Delivery, Technology leadership, and Product on portfolio strategy, retailer signal, and roadmap adoption.
 This is a roll-up-your-sleeves leadership opportunity for someone who has personally led the transformation of CS from reactive enablement toward proactive business advisory, can hire and develop senior consultative talent, and thrives in a fast-paced, BD-led commercial environment with shared standards rather than rigid process. The role reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Solutions , and is remote across the United States and Canada with a preference for proximity to Toronto for key cross-functional collaboration.
 About the Job
 Lead the Customer Success organization for the Enterprise Solutions portfolio — owning value realization, outcomes end to end, and partner closely with BD, who owns NRR, GRR, and expansion, by providing account health, risk signal, and expansion readiness.Build and develop a senior consultative CS bench by hiring, sponsoring, and ramping Customer Success Managers who engage with retailer executives on ecommerce strategy, merchandising, and operations and who can credibly influence retailer P&L outcomes and roadmap adoption.
 Manage senior managers leading segments, setting standards for what good looks like across the CSM’s — including QBR quality, growth planning, executive engagement, and renewal execution.
 Operate in a BD-led commercial environment as a true commercial peer to BD — preserving BD's ownership of the primary commercial relationship while owning post-sale accountability and surfacing churn, expansion, and escalation signal early and clearly.
 Partner with the Director of Enterprise Architecture & Engineering on shared-account coordination — ensuring the cross-org account team ( CS + Technical Account Managers (TAM’s) ) functions as one team to the retailer despite the functional ownership, with co-authored protocols and clean escalation paths.
 Define and enforce the CSM/TAM boundary based on segmentation — CSM’s lead retailer-executive engagement, value realization, and growth planning, while TAM’s own technical delivery, configuration, and issue resolution, so that CSM capacity stays focused on strategic advisory, not technical execution.
 Own the consultative transformation roadmap — talent strategy, comp structure, operating cadence, and tooling shifts required to evolve CS from a feature-enablement function into a strategic business advisory function.
 Partner with the Director of Retailer Delivery on the implementation-to-success motion as a managed lifecycle (not a document handoff) — ensuring CS is engaged early, named handoff criteria are met, and accounts transition cleanly into early-lifecycle growth ownership.
 Operationalize the retailer segmented model in CS — applying high-touch coverage and scaled/digital-first models, with clear exception protocols and capacity guardrails.
 Build a structured retailer-signal feedback loop into Product — using CS engagements to surface durable patterns (not anecdotes), instrument adoption of roadmap items, and hold CS accountable for adoption outcomes.
 Apply AI augmentation to scale CS coverage and quality without linear headcount growth — including health monitoring, account-prep automation, QBR/insight generation, and signal triage — partnering with the Technical org on tooling roadmap and adoption.
 Represent the post-sale narrative for the portfolio to senior leadership — integrating retention, growth, churn risk, executive-account temperature, and pipeline outlook — and serve as the Director-level escalation point for retailer relationships when CSM-led engagement is insufficient.
 About You
 Minimum Qualifications
 8+ years of enterprise customer success, account management, or post-sale leadership at a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.
 Direct, accountable leadership of a customer success organization responsible for adoption velocity, time-to-value, health score, at-risk portfolio, CSAT, QBR quality and support BD with GRR, NRR, and expansion.
 Track record of managing managers with demonstrated ability to set standards and develop senior leaders without micromanagement.
 Ownership of a CS book of business or post-sale P&L of meaningful scale (e.g., $1000M+ ARR) with documented outcomes on Adoption, NRR, GRR, or expansion.
 Proven success operating in a BD- or Sales-led commercial environment — clear instinct for where the CS lane begins and ends, comfort with shared standards rather than rigid RACI/process.
 Demonstrated executive presence with enterprise customer counterparts (VP / SVP / C-level), including the ability to deliver hard news, navigate escalations, and rebuild trust after issues.
 Experience designing and operating segmented CS coverage models (high-touch for strategic accounts, scaled/digital for the long tail), including capacity planning and exception handling.
 Hands-on experience hiring senior CS talent — with a clear point of view on profile, comp, and ramp.
 Strong background having operated in an end to end post sales service delivery ecosystem with strong CS interaction with Business Development/Sales, Delivery, Technical and Product teams. Preferred Qualifications
 Experience transforming a CS function from reactive enablement into proactive business advisory, including the talent, comp, operating-model, and tooling changes required (not a renaming exercise).
 Track record of building or scaling seasoned strategist roles inside a CS org — including hiring profile, ramp, comp design, and integration with the rest of the account team.
 Experience operating with a separate technical TAM function on shared enterprise accounts — including co-authoring cross-org protocols and managing escalations across an org boundary.
 Background applying AI to CS workflows — health monitoring, account preparation, QBR generation, signal triage — with measurable impact on coverage, throughput, or quality.
 Familiarity with the BD/CS interface in commercially complex enterprise sales motions, including renewals, multi-product expansion, and shared-account operating norms.
 Deep familiarity with enterprise retail, grocery, ecommerce platforms, retail media, or adjacent complex B2B domains — including how large retailers evaluate, adopt, and scale technology solutions.
 Experience instrumenting retailer signal into structured product feedback (not anecdotal) and partnering with Product leaders on adoption accountability.

 As Director (Head) of Customer Success Management, you own the post-launch merchant relationship for every Portless merchant and the team that delivers it. You lead the Customer Success Management motions, including onboarding & lifecycle teams.  You are the owner of Gross and Net Revenue Retention for the merchant base, and set the coverage model, playbooks, and cadences that turn the customer success flywheel (Adopt → Realize Value → Expand → Renew with Confidence) into a repeatable system across the Enterprise, Strategic, and Growth segments.
 This is a player-coach leadership role in a 0-to-1 environment. You will build the retention forecast leadership runs on, coach CSMs into commercially credible advisors, and partner with Technical Solutions, Operations, Product, Sales, and RevOps so that what we promise a merchant in a business review is what happens on the warehouse floor. You serve as an accountable partner in the success of our merchants and the Portless team members who support them.

 1. Team Leadership & Talent
 Build & Coach the Team: Hire, onboard, and develop CSMs & Hypercare managers (onboarding CSMs) across segments. Run weekly 1:1s, recorded call reviews (Gong), and a coaching cadence tied to a documented CSM competency model.
 Capacity & Book Design: Set book-of-business size and revenue coverage per CSM by segment, and re-balance books quarterly as merchants graduate from Hypercare or change tier.
 Performance Management: Define scorecards (retention, attach rate, health-score coverage, business review cadence) and hold the team to them with clear expectations and clear support.
 2. Retention, Forecasting & Risk Leadership
 Own GRR and NRR: Deliver Gross and Net Revenue Retention for the merchant base and publish a monthly retention forecast with named at-risk accounts, dollar exposure, and save plans.
 Risk Register Cadence: Run the weekly at-risk review. Every Yellow or Red account has a root cause, an owner, a dated next step, and an executive sponsor where needed.
 Churn Post-Mortems: Lead a written post-mortem within 10 business days of any logo loss or volume loss in the Enterprise and Strategic segments, and convert findings into playbook, operations, or product changes.
 Executive Escalations: Serve as the senior escalation point for Enterprise and Strategic merchants, driving root cause and corrective action across Operations, Technical Solutions, and Engineering.
 3. Coverage Model & Lifecycle Design
 Segmented Coverage: Design and run tiered engagement for Enterprise, Strategic, and Growth merchants, including a digital and pooled motion for the long tail so high-touch time goes where revenue and risk concentrate.
 Hypercare to CSM Graduation: Own the handoff standard from the four-phase Hypercare program (Stabilization → Enablement → Optimization → Graduation) into lifecycle CSM ownership, including handoff brief quality, a ≥90% graduation rate, and Peak Readiness: Lead merchant-facing peak planning (BFCM, Chinese New Year) with Operations: volume forecasts by merchant, inventory positioning, carrier mix, and surcharge communications delivered on a published calendar.
 4. Value Realization & Merchant Outcomes
 Health Scoring on Leading Indicators: Partner with CS Operations to design and maintain a merchant health score built on volume trend, exception rate, SLA attainment, stockout risk, invoice disputes, and engagement, and use it to trigger plays rather than to describe history.
 Executive Business Reviews: Set the standard for MBRs/QBRs/EBRs that quantify merchant outcomes in the merchant's terms (cost per order, delivery speed by country, cash flow released, exception rate) and end with agreed priorities and owners.
 Voice of the Merchant Program: Own the merchant sentiment system: risk scoring as the primary operating signal, Customer Effort Score at the transaction level, and decision-maker NPS as the relationship instrument, each with a defined response path and owner.
 5. Expansion via Services (Expand)
 Service Attach Rate: Own attach-rate targets and the expansion playbook for Portless services and partner solutions (Onward package protection, OpenBorder tax and duty compliance, Portless Capital inventory financing, US fulfillment expansion), with triggers, messaging, and objection handling documented for every play.
 Commercial Rigor: Coach CSMs on services-led discovery and business cases with clear merchant ROI. Partner with Sales on commercial terms and pipeline hygiene so influenced expansion is tracked in HubSpot, not in memory.
 Share-of-Wallet Growth: Identify merchants shipping a portion of their volume elsewhere and build the win-back and expansion motion with Sales and Operations.
 6. Systems, Data & Cross-Functional Leadership
 HubSpot as System of Record: Set and enforce data standards (health, phase, renewal, and expansion fields) so forecasts and dashboards can be trusted without manual reconciliation.
 AI-Assisted CS Operations: Deploy AI tooling where it removes CSM toil (call summaries, business review prep, anomaly alerts on volume and exceptions, draft merchant communications) and set the quality bar for when a human must review before anything reaches a merchant.
 Product & Operations Feedback Loop: Convert recurring merchant friction into ranked, evidenced requests to Product and Operations, and close the loop back to merchants when changes ship.
 Cross-Functional Accountability: Partner with the Head of Technical Solutions on implementation handoffs, with Account Champions in the China and Chicago FCs on Tier 1 and Tier 2 execution, and with RevOps on CS Ops tooling and reporting.

 Retention: Gross Revenue Retention at or above 90%, logo churn below 95%, and retention forecast accuracy within 10% points of actual.
 Growth: Net Revenue Retention above 100%, service attach rate of 15%, and influenced expansion pipeline and closed-won revenue tracked in HubSpot.
 Lifecycle: ≥90% Hypercare graduation rate, Sentiment: Decision-maker NPS at or above 50 (in collaboration with all of Portless leadership), with every detractor contacted within 5 business days.
 Team: New CSMs carrying a full book within 90 days, voluntary CSM attrition below 10%, and a documented competency model with quarterly calibration.

 You have led CSM teams through a retention turnaround or a scale-up and can show the before-and-after numbers. About the company 
 Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. This is a task-based, independent contractor opportunity, not an employment relationship. Participation is limited to this project.
 Project Highlights 
 Earnings per approved task: a fixed rate for each task, set in advance
 Fully self-scheduled: no minimum hours and no set schedule; you choose which tasks to take and when
 Remote: open to US-licensed physicians based in eligible US states
 No patient contact, no malpractice exposure: you review written clinical cases
 All contributors are license-verified physicians
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved
 What this project involves 
 We're looking for physicians (MD/DO) with an active, unrestricted US medical license to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation project. General and internal medicine are the main focus. Each task is a written clinical case, assessed against the project's acceptance criteria. Contributors may:
 Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor "trap" answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
 Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
 Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales.
 Each case receives three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You're improving the AI tools you'll eventually use yourself.
 What we look for 
 This project is a good fit for US-licensed physicians looking for a flexible, time-limited project they can fit around their other commitments. Ideally, contributors will have:
 Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified at onboarding and re-checked monthly);
 Board certification or completed residency training, with direct patient care experience (attending-level preferred). Practising or retired physicians welcome;
 Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
 Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
 Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
 Strong written English (C1+).
 This project is not suitable for medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.
 How it works 
 Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join the project → Complete tasks → Get paid for approved tasks
 Flexibility 
 You decide whether, when, and how much to contribute. There are no minimum hours, set schedules, or required availability. Task availability varies with project phases. Tasks are submitted through the platform and are approved when they meet the project’s acceptance criteria.
 Earnings 
 Earnings are paid only for completed and approved tasks. Each task type has a fixed rate. There is no time tracking and no hour logging. There are no tiers or speed adjustments to the rate. QA and adjudication tasks have a higher per-task rate.
 $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved.
 Quality incentives: additional earnings for high-quality approved tasks, on terms set out in the project guidelines.

 What’s in store for you?
 A rewarding job where you can enjoy the summer and cultivate in unique locations.
 A competitive salary.
 Free coffee and tea, and a workspace in the heart of Vancouver.
 A team-focused work environment that encourages initiative and leadership.
 Happy hours and various social events throughout the year.
 Fun team-building activities with your colleagues — because MicroHabitat is first and foremost a big family!

 Setting up agriculture projects.
 Managing production areas.
 Monitoring, supporting, and evaluating urban agriculture activities for assigned projects throughout the season.
 Collaborating with the MicroHabitat team to contribute to the expansion of the company worldwide and the deployment of urban agriculture in each of our cities.

 Procure supplies.

 Write reports and document activities for each production space.
 Perform tasks related to purchasing and maintaining tools and infrastructure.
 Conduct quality control and generate reports for managing the roofs of urban farms.

 Participate in the creation of standardization documents and training guides for company operations.
 Work directly with different company branches (sales and marketing) and with other cities where MicroHabitat operates.

 Participatory leadership.

 Interpersonal skills, relational abilities, and communication.

 Professional certifications such as CISSP, SailPoint, or related credentials.  
 Experience operating within healthcare, pharmaceutical, or other highly regulated industries.

 Knowledge of Zero Trust architecture, Privileged Access Management (PAM), and regulatory frameworks including SOX and HIPAA.

DIRECTOR, OPERATIONS

Level: M4 | Proficient
Location: Ottawa, ON | Hybrid 
Reports To: Victoria Wnek, VP, Operations https://www.linkedin.com/in/victoriachechui
Type: Permanent | Full-Time




ABOUT SOLINK

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!




THE ROLE

As Director, Operations, you'll own Solink's end-to-end sales-to-deployment operating model, from the moment a deal closes to the point a customer is live, supported and generating recurring revenue. Our Deployment function has grown in scale, complexity and strategic importance, and this role exists to lead it into its next chapter.

You'll lead a team across three focus areas: Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Operations Enablement. You'll be accountable for the overall function and driving major automation and process-improvement initiatives and partnering with senior leaders across the organization to improve planning, quality, scalability and accountability.

This is an opportunity for an operations leader who's energized by building systems that scale, raising the bar on execution and connecting operational performance directly to ARR growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the sales-to-deployment operating model: Define and continuously improve how work flows from Sales through Deployment to Support, including handoffs, planning, capacity, quality standards and accountability at every stage.

 - Lead and develop a high-performing leadership team: Lead Managers across Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Enablement & Cross-Functional. Set clear goals, coach for growth and build a leadership bench that can scale with the business.

 - Drive operational transformation: Lead major automation, tooling and process-improvement initiatives that increase throughput, reduce cycle time and improve the customer deployment experience.

 - Deliver on ARR: Ensure deployments are executed on time and at quality so that contracted revenue converts to recurring revenue predictably. Own the metrics, forecasting and reporting that connect operations to financial outcomes.

 - Partner across the organization: Work closely with senior leaders in Sales, Customer Success, Support, Product and Finance to align on planning, resolve cross-functional friction and make Deployment a strategic lever for the business.

 - Establish governance and operational rigour: Set the standards, SOPs, KPIs and reporting cadence that give leadership clear visibility into deployment health, capacity and risk.

 - Oversee partner and field strategy: Guide how Solink works with installation partners and field resources, including partner enablement, performance management and relationship health.

 - Serve as the senior escalation point: Own resolution of high-impact customer and operational escalations, and turn recurring issues into systemic fixes.




ROLE EXPECTATIONS

This is an M4 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level serve as a strategic advisor within a department, who is confident acting as their executive leader’s right hand within their functional area and is able to set cross-functional direction in collaboration with departments within the organization.



In this role, you'll be expected to:

 - Set the vision and multi-quarter roadmap for the Deployment function and translate it into clear priorities for your managers.

 - Operate with a high degree of autonomy, making decisions that shape how the function runs and how it interacts with the rest of the business.

 - Influence senior stakeholders across functions, building alignment on shared goals, processes and trade-offs.

 - Balance near-term delivery with long-term investment in automation, tooling and scalability.

 - Build a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement across the Deployment team.

What success looks like:

 - Deployment cycle times, on-time delivery and quality metrics improve measurably, and ARR from new deals is realized faster and more predictably.

 - Key automation and process-improvement initiatives are delivered, reducing manual effort and allowing the function to scale without proportional headcount growth.

 - Sales, Deployment, Support and other partners operate from a shared planning model with clear handoffs, visible accountability and fewer escalations.


WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Have:

 - 8+ years in operations, deployment, implementation or professional services, including 3+ years leading managers or multi-team functions.

 - A proven track record of designing and scaling an end-to-end operating model in a high-growth B2B technology, SaaS or hardware-enabled services environment.

 - Demonstrated success leading process-improvement and automation initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency, quality or revenue.

 - Strong analytical and business acumen, with experience owning KPIs, capacity planning and operational reporting tied to financial outcomes such as ARR.

 - Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the credibility to influence senior leaders and drive alignment.

Nice-to-Have:

 - Experience in physical security, video surveillance, IoT or other field-deployed technology.

 - Experience managing installation partner or channel networks across multiple regions.

 - Familiarity with operations tooling and automation platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Asana, Jira, n8n or similar).

 - Background in Lean, Six Sigma or other formal continuous-improvement methodologies.




SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

 - Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.


COMPENSATION

The compensation range for this role is $156,696-195,870 CAD and includes a base salary plus a performance-based variable component.

We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role.

For this position, we are hiring within the Proficient range. Candidates in this range will demonstrate the ability to serve as a strategic advisor within their department, confidently acting as the senior leader's right hand within their functional area and setting cross-functional direction in collaboration with other departments across the organization.




OUR VALUES

We do things the Solink way:

 - Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.

 - Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.

 - Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.

 - Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.
   

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.




WHY SOLINK?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

 - Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.

 - Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.

 - Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.

 - Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.

 - Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.

 - Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.

 - Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.




WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE HIRING PROCESS

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

 1. Intro call with our Talent Team

 2. Behavioural interview with a member of People & Culture

 3. Hiring Manager interview with this role's manager

 4. Cross-functional panel interview

 5. Reference Checks

 6. Offer & onboarding 🎉


PLEASE NOTE: THIS IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE AT ANY POINT IN THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THE BUSINESS.




HOW TO APPLY

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page https://solink.com/careers/]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.


NOTICE: SOLINK USES ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TO SCREEN, ASSESS, AND/OR SELECT CANDIDATES FOR THIS POSITION.




SOLINK IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER. WE’RE COMMITTED TO BUILDING A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE WORKPLACE. IF YOU REQUIRE ACCOMMODATION DURING THE SELECTION PROCESS, PLEASE LET US KNOW.

About AI Acquisition 
 AI Acquisition is a bootstrapped, founder-led business helping founders and operators scale with AI, combining a sales and delivery engine, one-to-one consultation, and our own SaaS platforms. We move fast, we build constantly, and we hold a high bar for the people who work directly with our clients.
 We currently manage thousands of active clients across multiple products, with 250+ new clients onboarding every month. The Account Management function is the front line of that relationship.
 The Role 
 You are the person between the client and the outcome. Not a relationship manager. Not a check-in scheduler. Not someone who forwards tickets and hopes for the best.
 You own a portfolio of clients who are building real businesses with our support. Some are launching for the first time. Some are scaling. Some are stuck and frustrated. Your job is to diagnose where they actually are, figure out what's blocking their progress, manage their expectations when needed, and drive them toward commercial results, not just activity.
 This means you need to understand marketing, sales, offer development, and fulfillment well enough to have real conversations about all of them. If a client's campaign is generating calls but nobody's closing, you need to be able to tell them why and what to do about it, not pass it to someone else.
 Our clients purchase a fully built AI lead-generation business: brand, website, funnel, lead engine, and the systems that help turn leads into customers. You own the relationship around that delivery. You need to know what they bought, what was promised, where they are in the journey, and what needs to happen next, with specifics, not generalities.
 You'll work directly with clients on Zoom, Slack, and through our internal systems. You'll run growth workshops, intro calls, and quick syncs. You'll manage escalations without panicking and celebrate wins without coasting. And when a client is about to walk, you'll be the person who finds the path to keep them or makes the honest call that they should go.
 What You'll Own: 
 A portfolio of active clients across different stages: onboarding, growth, scale, and at-risk
 Growth workshops, intro calls, and regular check-ins; you set the rhythm, not the client
 Client expectation management, framing what's realistic, resetting when needed, never overpromising
 Diagnosing why a client isn't getting results: is it the offer, the funnel, the sales process, the client's own execution, or something upstream?
 Funnel and campaign literacy and understanding the client's lead engine (Meta ads, cold email, B2B book-a-call, DFY website), confirming it matches their contract and guarantee, and flagging mismatches before they become problems
 Reading the client's specific contract, understanding the distinct payment flows (client pays AIA, client's customers pay client, ad spend reimbursement), and giving accurate answers under pressure rather than quoting generic numbers
 Spotting the signals before a client escalates (sudden silence, short replies, frustration, refund language, contract/funnel mismatches) and acting on them with a structured escalation, not a panicked message
 De-escalating frustrated clients without throwing the company under the bus, without panicking, and without making promises you can't keep
 When you inherit accounts, you verify every client's status, contract, delivery stage, and risk level before assuming anything is fine
 Spotting when a client is ready for more and positioning it as the natural next step, not a sales pitch
 Every client interaction, decision, and next step logged in our systems (Athena ticketing, Slack channels)
 Collaboration with the broader CS, delivery, and onboarding teams to make sure nothing falls through the cracks
 What We Need From You 
 4+ years in a client-facing account management, CSM, or business consulting role where you were directly responsible for client outcomes, not just client satisfaction scores
 You've consulted business owners on how to start, grow, or scale a business, walked them through the hard parts, not just handed them a playbook
 You understand (or can learn fast) the mechanics of B2B lead generation: Meta ads, cold email campaigns, funnels, and how they connect to a client's revenue. You don't need to run campaigns yourself, but you need to diagnose why one isn't converting and have a real conversation about it with the client
 You're comfortable navigating money conversations with clients, not quoting generic numbers, but reading the specific contract, understanding the payment flows, and giving accurate answers under pressure
 You can manage difficult client conversations with composure, you stay calm, you don't blame, you find the path forward
 You come with solutions, not just problems. When something breaks, your instinct is to propose a fix, not report the issue and wait
 You're confident on camera and on calls; clients trust people who sound like they know what they're doing, even under pressure
 You've worked in a startup, agency, or fast-moving environment where things change fast and you had to figure things out without a manual
 You're comfortable with AI tools and either already use them in your workflow or are the kind of person who finds and tests them without being told to
 You don't need to be chased. You manage your own time, your own portfolio, and your own follow-ups
 This Is Not For You If: 
 You only know one side of the equation (only marketing, or only sales) and aren't interested in learning the other
 You need everything documented before you can act; we're building the playbook, not following one
 You wait for clients to come to you with problems instead of spotting them early
 You avoid hard conversations or default to telling clients what they want to hear
 You treat AI as a buzzword rather than something you actually use
 You need heavy management and regular direction to stay productive
 You hear "refund" and freeze instead of diagnosing what went wrong and whether it's fixable
 What Success Looks Like: 
 Your clients are progressing; not just happy, but actually hitting milestones and getting results
 Escalations that reach you don't reach anyone above you, you resolve them
 You're the AM other people point to when asked "who handles clients well here"
 You identify upsell opportunities because you actually understand where the client is and what they need next
 Clients at risk are flagged before they ask for a refund, not after
 You can audit a new book of business end to end and produce an accurate status picture within your first week of owning it
 Your documentation is clean, current, and useful; anyone picking up your account can see exactly where things stand
 You adopt new tools and processes fast and bring ideas for improving them
 Our Process 
 After an initial screen, you'll complete a scenario-based Loom task, a real client situation that tests how you diagnose problems, manage expectations, and make commercial decisions. If you pass, you'll meet with our CS Leadership team for a deeper conversation.
 We assess for judgment, not just experience. Show us how you think.
 The Environment 
 This is a high-performance, remote-first team operating at the cutting edge of AI-powered business building. Here's what that means for you:
 Direct access to founders from day one, no layers, no politics. You'll work alongside people who are building the business, not managing from a distance.
 Real growth path, strong performers are promoted from month three, not year three. We move people up based on what they deliver, not how long they've been here.
 Exposure to AI-led systems and tools, you won't just use AI as a buzzword on your CV. You'll operate inside a business that builds and ships AI products daily, and you'll be expected to use them to get better at your job.
 Compensation that rewards output, base plus performance bonus plus upsell commission. The harder you push, the more you earn.
 Autonomy and ownership, you manage your portfolio, your time, and your client relationships. No micromanagement, no hand-holding.
 A team that holds a high bar, the people around you are operators, not passengers. That's the standard, and it's what makes this place worth being in.
If you're looking for structure handed to you, this isn't the right place. If you want to be the one " Lifting up the hood ", build something real, and raise the bar every week with a team that moves fast - we want to talk.

Vision Suite and FarsightIQ cover merchandising, planning, supply chain, and omni-channel operations on a single master data foundation. Les conseiller·ères en acquisition de talents et mobilité interne jouent un rôle essentiel dans la recherche, l'attraction, l'évaluation et la sélection des meilleurs talents externes et internes pour l'organisation. En tant que conseiller·ères en mobilité interne, iels jouent un rôle essentiel en facilitant l'évolution de carrière et les opportunités de développement pour les employés au sein de l'entreprise, en s'appuyant sur leur connaissance approfondie des communautés d'expertise dont iels s'occupent et des besoins spécifiques des projets. 
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Élaborer des stratégies de recrutement et des processus de sélection pour répondre aux besoins de recrutement de tous les studios de la zone.
 Soutenir et guider les gestionnaires pour répondre à leurs besoins en recrutement, en agissant en tant que conseiller de confiance en ce qui concerne la sélection des talents. 
 Accompagner les candidats et les employés tout au long du processus de sélection + documenter les interactions, les suivis et les négociations.
Ce que vous apportez à l’équipe 
 Mapping des talents : Les conseillers en TA&IM doivent avoir une connaissance approfondie du vivier de talents et des compétences de l'organisation afin de pouvoir mettre en adéquation les candidats internes et les postes à pourvoir. Ils doivent être au fait des tendances du secteur, du contexte concurrentiel et de l'évolution de la dynamique du marché des talent afin d'affiner les stratégies de recrutement.
 Évaluation et sélection des candidats : Capacité à évaluer les qualifications, les compétences et l'expérience des candidats afin de déterminer s'ils sont qualifiés pour des postes précis. Ils sont compétents pour créer des processus de sélection structurés, y compris des entretiens efficaces, et pour évaluer les capacités des candidats. 
 Connaissance de l'organisation : Une connaissance approfondie de la structure de l'entreprise, de ses départements, de ses fonctions et de ses rôles est essentielle. Les conseillers doivent être en mesure d'identifier les profils potentiels des candidats par rapport aux postes à pourvoir. Ils doivent fournir des conseils sur la manière dont les employés peuvent progresser et évoluer au sein de l'entreprise en s'appuyant sur des outils et des cadres développés spécifiquement pour la mobilité de carrière. 
 Compétences en négociations : Capacité à négocier la rémunération et les offres d'emploi afin d'obtenir les meilleurs candidats tout en respectant l'équité interne et les critères C&B. De plus, la mobilité interne implique souvent de convaincre les collaborateurs d'accepter un poste prioritaire qui n'est pas forcément celui qu'ils préfèrent. Les conseillers doivent avoir les compétences nécessaires pour négocier des options de recrutement avec les collaborateurs dans de tels scénarios, afin de garantir que les priorités de l'entreprise soient comblées. 
 Gestion de la rétroaction : Fournir une rétroaction constructive aux candidats et aux employés d'une manière professionnelle et constructive, quel que soit le résultat.

About AmpThink 
 AmpThink is a Master Technology Integrator — we design and deploy the technology behind many of North America’s premier sports and entertainment venues, spanning wired and wireless networking, LED and large-format displays, IPTV, and audio/visual systems. Our customers include major sports organizations such as Maple Leafs Sports & Entertainment, the Calgary Flames, and the Buffalo Bills. Our Canadian operations run from our office in Fort Erie, Ontario, working hand-in-hand with our head office in Garland, Texas.
 The Role 
 We are hiring a Full-Charge Bookkeeper to serve as the lead of our Canadian office in Fort Erie, reporting directly to AmpThink’s CFO in Garland, Texas. You will own the complete set of Canadian books, run the day-to-day of the office, and be our on-the-ground financial contact for “all things Canada.” It is an accounting-led role with a light set of office-management duties on top — and it comes with real ownership: you lead the Canadian office. Because AmpThink builds the technology inside major sports and entertainment venues, the books you keep sit behind real projects at real venues.
 This is a genuinely cross-border opportunity. You will maintain a Canadian set of books that reports up to a U.S. parent — reconciling intercompany activity, working in both CAD and USD, and bridging Canadian requirements (GST/HST and CRA payroll remittances) with U.S. head-office processes. If you enjoy operating at the intersection of two countries’ accounting and tax systems, this role offers that variety every day.
 AmpThink’s Canadian Practice lead is based here in Fort Erie but travels frequently, so day to day you will often be the on-site presence keeping the office and the books running — with the Practice lead and our U.S. finance team a call away. This is an on-site role well suited to someone in the Niagara region who wants a stable seat close to home, without the daily commute to Toronto — and, for a sports fan, the Buffalo Bills are right across the border.
 The ideal candidate is an experienced full-charge bookkeeper — ideally with construction or project-based experience (job costing, work-in-progress, progress billing) — who wants the autonomy of leading a small office close to home. A CPA is welcome but not required; strong, hands-on bookkeeping is what matters.
 This is a newly created position. 
 What You Will Do 
 Own the full cycle of accounting for the Canadian entity — accounts payable and receivable, bank and general-ledger reconciliations, and journal entries — and support month-end and year-end close with clean, organized records
 Prepare and remit Canadian GST/HST and payroll source deductions to the CRA, or coordinate them with head office and external advisors
 Work across the border with head office in Garland, Texas — reconcile intercompany activity, handle CAD/USD transactions, and keep U.S. leadership current on Canadian financial matters
 Assist with US bookkeeping and accounting in partnership with the CFO as time allows
 Track recurring charges, review and code incoming bills, and route them to the right approvers
 Help schedule field resources and track their time, attendance, and expenses in AmpThink’s Zoho tools
 Keep the small Fort Erie office running — mail, supplies, vendors, filing, and records
 Occasionally receive materials at the loading dock — sign for deliveries, move items with a manual pallet jack, and lift up to 50 lbs (23 kg)
 How We Use AI in This Process 
 AmpThink uses artificial intelligence to help screen and assess applications against the criteria for this role. AI does not make the final decision: our CFO reviews every application, with the benefit of that AI analysis, before any candidate is ruled out.
 What You Bring 
 Strong, hands-on full-charge bookkeeping experience — a complete set of books: AP/AR, reconciliations, journal entries, and month-end close
 Construction or project-based accounting experience — job costing, work-in-progress (WIP), progress billing, and holdback/retainage (strongly preferred)
 Working knowledge of Canadian GST/HST and payroll source-deduction / CRA remittances
 Proficiency with a cloud accounting/ERP system and strong Excel skills — we run on Zoho (Books, People, Projects, Expense); QuickBooks, Sage, or Xero experience transfers well
 Comfort working across CAD and USD and coordinating with a U.S. head office
 Genuine comfort leading a small office on your own — self-directed, organized, and reliable, since the Canadian Practice lead travels frequently
 A willingness to carry light office-management duties — mail, receiving, and coordination — alongside the books
 Able to lift up to 50 lbs (23 kg) and operate a manual pallet jack for occasional receiving
 Clear written and verbal communication
 Legally entitled to work in Canada; able to pass a background and reference check
 Nice to Have 
 CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant) designation, or active progress toward one — welcome, not required
 Experience in a sports, venue, or large-project environment
 Cross-border or intercompany experience, or exposure to both Canadian and U.S. tax and reporting
 Experience with multi-currency (CAD/USD) transactions and reconciliations
 Experience running the books for a small entity, branch, or solo office
 Familiarity with the Zoho suite

We’re building the next generation of agentic AI infrastructure at Cohere. This team sits at the intersection of ML systems, distributed infrastructure, and developer experience, creating the platform that powers autonomous AI agents at scale.

You’ll work on hard, forward-looking problems with few established patterns, including secure code execution, agent state management, model routing, identity and authentication, and resource management for long-running agent workflows.

 - State management, memory, and filesystem abstractions for agents.

 - Prototype and evaluate new technologies, then help decide what should move into production

 - Partner with research teams to shape infrastructure based on what future agent systems will need

 - Familiarity with model routing and LLM provider frameworks across different model types and environments

 - Experience with scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems and Kubernetes

BONUS

Le rôle est responsable de l’intégrité, de l’exactitude et de l’évolutivité des activités comptables mondiales de l’entreprise, y compris la clôture financière et la production de rapports, la comptabilisation des revenus, les comptes clients, les comptes fournisseurs, les contrôles financiers, la comptabilité statutaire et les activités financières connexes.
 Il s’agit d’un rôle de leadership à la fois stratégique et concret. La personne retenue allie une solide expertise technique en comptabilité à un leadership opérationnel et renforcera les processus, les contrôles, les systèmes, la discipline de trésorerie et les capacités organisationnelles à mesure que Power Factors poursuit sa croissance à l’échelle mondiale. Le rôle contribuera à bâtir un modèle de contrôle financier évolutif qui soutient plusieurs entités, devises, juridictions et modèles commerciaux en évolution.
 CE QUE VOUS FEREZ
 Comptabilité mondiale et contrôle financier 
 Diriger la fonction mondiale de comptabilité et de contrôle financier de l’entreprise, en assurant une information financière exacte, à jour et uniforme dans l’ensemble des entités et des juridictions.
 Assumer la responsabilité des processus de clôture financière mensuelle, trimestrielle et annuelle et améliorer continuellement la rapidité, la qualité et la prévisibilité de la clôture.
 S’assurer que des politiques, procédures, contrôles, rapprochements et documents comptables appropriés sont en place dans toute l’organisation.
 Superviser les activités de comptabilité générale, y compris le grand livre, la comptabilité intersociétés, les charges à payer, les charges payées d’avance, les immobilisations et les rapprochements de bilan.
 Assurer l’application uniforme des politiques comptables dans les entités mondiales et repérer de façon proactive les risques comptables émergents.
 Information financière, gouvernance et conformité 
 Superviser la préparation et l’intégrité des états financiers consolidés et des rapports de gestion.
 Maintenir de solides contrôles financiers et une gouvernance appropriée des processus financiers, avec des responsabilités et des mécanismes d’escalade clairs.
 Diriger le processus d’audit externe et agir à titre de principal point de contact pour les auditeurs externes et les conseillers en comptabilité.
 Assurer la conformité aux normes comptables applicables et aux exigences de production de rapports statutaires dans les entités internationales.
 Collaborer avec les équipes Fiscalité, Affaires juridiques, Paie et Personnes et culture pour soutenir les exigences réglementaires, statutaires et de conformité des entités.
 Agir à titre de partenaire clé du ou de la chef·fe de la direction financière en matière de comptabilité, de gouvernance financière, de risque, d’évolutivité opérationnelle et de priorités de transformation des Finances.
 Comptabilisation des revenus 
 Diriger le cadre comptable d’un environnement de revenus mondial complexe couvrant les abonnements SaaS, les services professionnels, les projets, les ententes de mise en œuvre et d’autres contrats clients.
 Assumer la responsabilité des politiques de comptabilisation des revenus, des évaluations de contrats, des processus, des rapprochements et des contrôles, en assurant une application exacte et uniforme dans l’ensemble de l’entreprise. La connaissance de la comptabilisation des revenus au fil du temps selon l’ASC 606 est un atout.
 Collaborer avec les Opérations des revenus, la Planification et analyse financières (FP&A), les Ventes, les Services professionnels, les Affaires juridiques et d’autres équipes de l’entreprise pour assurer une information sur les revenus exacte et à jour.
 S’assurer que les contrats et ententes clients complexes sont évalués adéquatement sur le plan comptable.
 Renforcer les processus et les contrôles liés aux revenus à mesure que l’entreprise et ses modèles commerciaux évoluent.
 Opérations comptables et fonds de roulement 
 Assurer le leadership des comptes clients, des comptes fournisseurs, de la comptabilité générale et des opérations comptables connexes.
 Établir une solide discipline opérationnelle en matière de facturation, de recouvrement, d’affectation des encaissements, de paiements aux fournisseurs, de charges à payer et de rapprochements.
 Favoriser une performance efficace du fonds de roulement grâce à des responsabilités claires, des niveaux de service, des contrôles, des processus d’escalade et des indicateurs clés mesurables.
 S’assurer que les opérations comptables soutiennent efficacement plusieurs entités juridiques, devises et juridictions.
 Systèmes, processus, transformation et intégration 
 Bâtir un modèle opérationnel de contrôle financier mondial évolutif en normalisant les processus, en éliminant les activités manuelles inutiles, en renforçant l’utilisation des systèmes et en recourant à l’automatisation et à l’IA lorsque approprié.
 Renforcer l’utilisation des systèmes et des données financières afin d’améliorer l’exactitude, l’évolutivité, la transparence et le soutien à la prise de décisions.
 Collaborer avec les leaders des Finances et de l’entreprise pour simplifier les processus de bout en bout tout en maintenant des contrôles appropriés.
 Établir et suivre les principaux indicateurs de contrôle financier, y compris le cycle de clôture, la qualité des rapprochements, les comptes clients en souffrance, l’exactitude de la facturation, les constatations d’audit, l’efficacité des contrôles et l’efficience des processus.
 Soutenir la vérification diligente financière, la comptabilisation des acquisitions et l’intégration des entités, systèmes et processus acquis, au besoin.
 S’assurer que les processus et les systèmes sont évolutifs dans plusieurs entités, devises et juridictions, ainsi que pour la croissance future de l’entreprise.
 Leadership et organisation 
 Diriger, former et encadrer une organisation comptable répartie sur plusieurs régions géographiques.
 Bâtir une solide capacité de leadership, une profondeur technique et une relève au sein de l’équipe des Finances.
 Établir des responsabilités, des priorités, des droits de décision et des rythmes opérationnels clairs dans toute l’organisation de contrôle financier.
 Développer une organisation capable de concilier une gouvernance financière rigoureuse et un soutien réactif et pragmatique à l’entreprise.
 Collaborer étroitement avec le ou la chef·fe de la direction financière, la FP&A, les Opérations des revenus, la Fiscalité, les Affaires juridiques, Personnes et culture et les leaders opérationnels.

 12 ans et plus d’expérience progressive en comptabilité, en contrôle financier, en information financière ou dans des rôles de leadership connexes en finance.
 Expérience significative de leadership à titre de contrôleur·euse, de contrôleur·euse corporatif·ive, de vice-président·e Comptabilité ou dans un rôle senior de contrôle financier au sein d’une organisation mondiale complexe.
 Titre comptable professionnel tel que CPA, CA, CMA, ACCA ou l’équivalent.
 Solide expertise technique en comptabilité et en information financière, avec un bon jugement dans des situations complexes ou en évolution.
 Expérience de la direction d’opérations comptables dans plusieurs entités juridiques, devises et juridictions.
 Expérience démontrée de la gestion de la clôture mensuelle et de fin d’exercice, des audits externes, des contrôles financiers et de l’information statutaire.
 Bonne compréhension de la comptabilisation des revenus et expérience dans un environnement d’abonnement, SaaS, technologique ou de revenus tout aussi complexe, y compris des ententes comportant des volets de services ou de mise en œuvre.
 Expérience de la direction et du développement d’équipes financières réparties sur plusieurs régions géographiques.
 Succès démontré dans l’amélioration, la normalisation et l’automatisation des processus comptables et dans l’établissement d’indicateurs opérationnels significatifs.
 Solide expérience des ERP et des systèmes financiers; l’expérience avec NetSuite est fortement souhaitable.
 L’expérience du soutien aux acquisitions, de la comptabilisation des acquisitions ou de l’intégration après acquisition est un atout.
 Capacité à évoluer efficacement dans une organisation dynamique et en évolution, et à passer aisément du leadership stratégique aux enjeux opérationnels détaillés.
 Solides aptitudes de communication auprès de la direction et capacité à travailler efficacement avec les leaders, les auditeurs, les conseillers et les équipes interfonctionnelles.
 À QUOI RESSEMBLE LE SUCCÈS
 Des états financiers fiables : L’information financière est exacte, complète, bien contrôlée et sert de référence à la direction.

 Une solide discipline de trésorerie : Les processus de facturation, de recouvrement, de comptes fournisseurs, d’affectation des encaissements et de fonds de roulement fonctionnent avec des responsabilités claires et une performance mesurable.
 Des opérations évolutives : Les processus et systèmes comptables soutiennent une organisation SaaS mondiale multientité sans complexité manuelle inutile ni croissance disproportionnée des effectifs.
 Une gouvernance solide : Les risques comptables, les enjeux de contrôle, les constatations d’audit et les exigences de conformité sont repérés et traités de façon proactive.
 Un partenariat avec l’entreprise : L’organisation du contrôle financier allie la rigueur financière à une compréhension pragmatique de l’entreprise et favorise de saines prises de décisions.
 Une équipe très performante : L’organisation comptable mondiale compte des leaders solides, des responsabilités claires, une relève bien établie et les capacités requises pour la prochaine étape de croissance de Power Factors.
 LA VIE CHEZ POWER FACTORS
 Power Factors est une entreprise de développement logiciel agile, suffisamment structurée pour avoir un impact concret tout en demeurant flexible et réactive dans un secteur en forte croissance.  Power Factors is a software and solutions provider leading the next generation of clean energy with Unity, one of the most extensive and widely deployed Renewable Energy Management Suites (REMS) in the market.

 THE OPPORTUNITY
 Power Factors is seeking an experienced Vice President, Controller to lead the company's global accounting and controllership organization in a complex, international SaaS and technology environment.
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the VP, Controller is a key member of the Finance leadership team and a trusted partner to the CFO on accounting, financial governance, risk, operational scalability, and Finance transformation. The role is responsible for the integrity, accuracy, and scalability of the company's global accounting operations, including financial close and reporting, revenue accounting, accounts receivable, accounts payable, financial controls, statutory accounting, and related finance operations.
 This is both a strategic and hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting expertise with operational leadership and will strengthen processes, controls, systems, cash discipline, and organizational capabilities as Power Factors continues to grow globally. The role will help build a scalable controllership model that supports multiple entities, currencies, jurisdictions, and evolving commercial models.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Global Accounting & Controllership 
 Lead the company's global accounting and controllership function, ensuring accurate, timely, and consistent financial reporting across entities and jurisdictions.
 Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes and continuously improve the speed, quality, and predictability of the close.
 Ensure appropriate accounting policies, procedures, controls, reconciliations, and documentation are in place across the organization.
 Provide oversight of general accounting activities, including general ledger, intercompany accounting, accruals, prepayments, fixed assets, and balance sheet reconciliations.
 Ensure consistent application of accounting policies across global entities and proactively identify emerging accounting risks.
 Financial Reporting, Governance & Compliance 
 Oversee the preparation and integrity of consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
 Maintain strong financial controls and appropriate governance over financial processes, with clear ownership and escalation mechanisms.
 Lead the external audit process and serve as a key point of contact for external auditors and accounting advisors.
 Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and statutory reporting requirements across international entities.
 Partner with Tax, Legal, Payroll, and People & Culture to support regulatory, statutory, and entity compliance requirements.
 Act as a key partner to the CFO on accounting, financial governance, risk, operational scalability, and Finance transformation priorities.
 Revenue Accounting 
 Lead the accounting framework for a complex global revenue environment spanning SaaS subscriptions, professional services, projects, implementation arrangements, and other customer contracts.
 Own revenue recognition policies, contract assessments, processes, reconciliations, and controls, ensuring accurate and consistent application across the business. Familiarity with ASC 606 overtime revenue recognition is a plus.
 Partner with Revenue Operations, FP&A, Sales, Professional Services, Legal, and other business teams to ensure accurate and timely revenue reporting.
 Ensure complex customer arrangements and contracts are appropriately assessed from an accounting perspective.
 Strengthen revenue-related processes and controls as the business and its commercial models evolve.
 Accounting Operations & Working Capital 
 Provide leadership across Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, general accounting, and related accounting operations.
 Establish strong operational discipline around billing, collections, cash application, vendor payments, accruals, and reconciliations.
 Drive effective working-capital performance through clear ownership, service levels, controls, escalation processes, and measurable KPIs.
 Ensure accounting operations effectively support multiple legal entities, currencies, and jurisdictions.
 Systems, Processes, Transformation & Integration 
 Build a scalable global controllership operating model by standardizing processes, eliminating unnecessary manual activities, strengthening system utilization, and using automation and AI where appropriate.
 Strengthen the use of financial systems and data to improve accuracy, scalability, transparency, and decision support.
 Partner with Finance and business leaders to simplify end-to-end processes while maintaining appropriate controls.
 Establish and monitor key controllership metrics, including close cycle, reconciliation quality, aged receivables, billing accuracy, audit findings, control effectiveness, and process efficiency.
 Support financial due diligence, purchase accounting, and the integration of acquired entities, systems, and processes as required.
 Ensure processes and systems are scalable across multiple entities, currencies, jurisdictions, and future business growth.
 Leadership & Organization 
 Lead, develop, and mentor a geographically distributed accounting organization.
 Build strong leadership capability, technical depth, and succession within the Finance team.
 Establish clear accountability, priorities, decision rights, and operating rhythms across the controllership organization.
 Develop an organization capable of balancing strong financial governance with responsive, pragmatic support to the business.
 Partner closely with the CFO, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Tax, Legal, People & Culture, and operational leaders.
 WHAT YOU'LL NEED
 12+ years of progressive experience in accounting, controllership, financial reporting, or related finance leadership roles.
 Significant leadership experience in a Controller, Corporate Controller, VP Accounting, or senior controllership role within a complex, global organization.
 Professional accounting designation such as CPA, CA, CMA, ACCA, or equivalent.
 Strong technical accounting and financial reporting expertise, with sound judgment in complex or evolving situations.
 Experience leading accounting operations across multiple legal entities, currencies, and jurisdictions.
 Demonstrated experience managing month-end and year-end close, external audits, financial controls, and statutory reporting.
 Strong understanding of revenue recognition and experience in a subscription, SaaS, technology, or similarly complex revenue environment, including arrangements involving services or implementation components.
 Experience leading and developing geographically distributed finance teams.
 Demonstrated success improving, standardizing, and automating accounting processes and establishing meaningful operational metrics.
 Strong ERP and financial systems experience; experience with NetSuite is highly desirable.
 Experience supporting acquisitions, purchase accounting, or post-acquisition integration is an asset.
 Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving organization and move comfortably between strategic leadership and detailed operational issues.
 Strong executive communication skills and the ability to work effectively with leadership, auditors, advisors, and cross-functional teams.
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
 Trusted financials: Financial information is accurate, complete, well controlled, and relied upon by leadership.
 Predictable close: Month-end, quarter-end, and year-end processes are disciplined, timely, and increasingly automated.
 Strong cash discipline: Billing, collections, payables, cash application, and working-capital processes operate with clear ownership and measurable performance.
 Scalable operations: Accounting processes and systems support a global, multi-entity SaaS organization without unnecessary manual complexity or disproportionate headcount growth.
 Strong governance: Accounting risks, control issues, audit findings, and compliance requirements are identified and addressed proactively.
 Business partnership: The Controller organization combines financial discipline with a pragmatic understanding of the business and enables sound decision-making.
 High-performing team: The global accounting organization has strong leaders, clear accountability, succession depth, and the capabilities required for Power Factors' next stage of growth.

 We are an agile software development company, large enough to make an impact and small enough to move quickly within a rapidly growing industry. We are a team of passionate, innovative, and results-driven professionals committed to making the world a better place through technology and clean energy.

 By joining Power Factors, you will become part of a collaborative and mission-driven organization dedicated to accelerating the transition to renewable energy. We offer opportunities for growth, learning, and meaningful impact while working alongside talented colleagues around the globe.

 Power Factors is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work.  Sound judgement about which deals are real.

 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.

 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed.

 Build your own pipeline across your territory

 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well

 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.

 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.

 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role

 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.

L’ingénieur en test et conception mécanique conçoit les bancs d’essaies et supervise leur fabrication, prenant en charge l’achat de matériel, la coordination du personnel technique du laboratoire et la liaison avec les ingénieurs systèmes et/ou de conception des projets.

 DOF Canada is currently seeking a detailed oriented and client focused individual for the position of  Survey Party Chief. A key to success for this position is the ability to collaborate with offshore and onshore personnel. The Party Chief will report to the Project Manager. If you are looking for a dynamic environment to learn and grow your career, DOF Canada is a great opportunity!
 We are looking to expand our survey team to support ongoing long-term multi year international and local projects. Expected 4 to 6 week rotation.

 Supervising checking and testing of survey equipment and software prior to project
 Coordinating and managing the mobilisation of survey equipment and software on vessel
 Must have a full understanding of the flow of data from the calibration at the project mobilization, through the logging and quality control of all data
 Development of project procedures and assist in project preparation.
 Management of project work scope and adhering to the contractual aspects of the project offshore.
 Manage, provide guidance and supervise the Offshore survey team
 Ensure the work is performed with adequate equipment and personnel.
 Ensure all personnel meet the company requirements for operational capability, competence, health, and safety.
 Communicate, on a daily basis, with the Project Manager.
 Liaising with client representatives and senior vessel/ROV crew.
 Manage subcontractor’s field team.
 Responsible for carrying out offshore appraisals and encouraging / ensuring team development.
 Accountable for delegation of responsibility in accordance with company procedures, when appropriate.
 Must complete daily/end of project reporting.
 Responsible for Offshore QHSE.
 Implement and maintain survey standards throughout offshore operations.

 Liaise with the Project Manager to ensure a complete understanding of the commercial impact of all decisions made offshore.
 Key Qualifications and Experience: 
 Post Secondary Education in Hydrographic Survey or Geomatics degree or similar education  
 At  least  3 years of experience  as  a Senior Surveyor
 Key experience in acting Party Chief or Party Chief duties
 Proficiency in Microsoft Packages - Word/Excel/PowerPoint and Document Control Systems
 Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills
 Excellent communicator, reader, and writer.
 Incident Investigation & Reporting
 Leadership Communication

 DOF is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to promoting a diverse workforce and an inclusive respectful workplace. 
 We encourage applications from all qualified individuals. We thank all applicants for their interest but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 At the university, the Marketing and Communications function is responsible for enhancing and protecting the university’s reputation.  The Director, Digital Experience leads the University’s digital experience strategy and shared digital ecosystem. Serving as the University’s senior lead for digital experience, the Director establishes frameworks and governance to enable consistent execution across a decentralized environment.
