Who we are
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
 About the team 
 Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.
 Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.
 Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue.
 What you’ll do
 As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.
 You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve.
 Responsibilities 
 Build and operate reliable, low-latency services that detect and prevent fraud and abuse at scale
 Design APIs and dashboard experiences that help businesses investigate threats, configure defenses, and understand how Radar protects them
 Develop the shared platform and infrastructure that enable teams to build and launch new Radar capabilities
 Work directly with users to understand emerging threats and turn those insights into broadly useful products
 Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to bring new signals, models, and AI capabilities into production
 Own projects end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and iteration
 Uphold a high bar for engineering quality, reliability, and product craft while moving quickly as threats evolve
 Who you are
 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 Minimum requirements 
 2+ years of industry software engineering experience
 Strong coding skills in any programming language, with experience building and maintaining production software
 Ability to work across systems and technologies, learn unfamiliar codebases, and make thoughtful technical trade-offs
 A rigorous approach to problem solving, including using data to investigate issues and evaluate whether a solution works
 Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across disciplines and contribute to your peers’ success
 An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems
 Preferred qualifications 
 Experience building distributed systems or real-time services with demanding reliability and latency requirements
 Experience building APIs, developer platforms, or intuitive user interfaces for complex workflows
 Experience bringing ML or AI capabilities into production software
 Experience working on fraud prevention, abuse prevention, risk, or security
 Experience taking a product from an early idea to launch and iterating directly with customers

Job Title: Senior Marketing Manager
 Primary Job Location: Hybrid, three days per week, Toronto / Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Ontario, Canada
 Employment Type: Permanent, Full-Time 
 Reporting Line: Chief Strategy Officer
 Team: Leads a small team of marketing specialists, with design support
 Travel: Up to 10 - 15%, for conferences and buyer events, including some US travel
 Hiring Timeline: Immediate
 Existing Vacancy: Yes
 Application Deadline: Open until filled. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
 Compensation: $115,000 - $135,000 CAD per year. Target performance bonus: 20% of base salary, tied to marketing-sourced qualified pipeline and bookings goals. Bonus eligibility begins with the 2027 plan year; plan details are provided at offer.
 About Fulfillment IQ
 Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations. 
 We work at the intersection of strategy, operations, and technology, solving complex, real-world problems across warehouse design, automation, order management, transportation, and end-to-end supply chain execution. Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk. 
 If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients and experts, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is a place where your skills and judgment come to life. 
 Marketing at FIQ 
 We are building a small, hands-on marketing team with one job: turn conferences and useful content into qualified conversations with the right buyers at brands, retailers and 3PLs. The team runs two motions: 
 Conference and buyer events: we attend a conference because the right buyers are there and a practice has a relevant offer, and we add dinners, roundtables or expert sessions when that improves access to those buyers. 
 Named-account campaigns: we pick accounts with our sellers, identify the buyer and a credible business problem, and reach them through content, organic LinkedIn, email, the website and coordinated seller outreach. 
 We do not run paid advertising. We work alongside an established media, editorial and community program (including the eCom Logistics Podcast and the CrossDock community), with in-house design support and a RevOps lead who owns HubSpot configuration and funnel reporting. We use AI extensively for research, drafting, repurposing and analysis, with human verification and clear accountability for every published claim. 
 The Role
 You will own FIQ's marketing-sourced qualified pipeline number and personally build the campaigns that produce it. You set the annual and quarterly marketing plan with the Chief Strategy Officer and Sales, then you write the briefs, build the HubSpot workflows, launch the campaigns, review the funnel every week and fix what is not working. You lead a small team of specialists and in-house designers, and you stay in the work yourself. 
 This is a player-coach role in a company that measures marketing by qualified pipeline, not by activity. You will have real authority over priorities, budget and campaign design, and real accountability for the result. 
 What this role is  
 Hands-on demand generation leadership for a B2B services and technology company selling to supply chain, logistics and 3PL buyers. 
 Accountable for a marketing-sourced qualified pipeline target agreed with Sales and the Chief Strategy Officer, and for the forecast behind it. 
 Owner of two motions: conference and city-based buyer events, and named-account campaigns supported by content, organic LinkedIn, email and the website. 
 Owner of the marketing plan, calendar, budget, campaign standards and the HubSpot funnel definitions marketing shares with Sales. 
 Manager and coach to a small team, with a RevOps lead, a Community & Media Lead and practice experts as close partners. 
 What this role is not  
 Not a brand or communications role. Brand consistency matters, but pipeline is the job. 
 Not a paid-media role. We do not run advertising and this is not expected to change in 2027. 
 Not an agency-management role. You and your team do the work. 
 Not a pure strategy role. If you have not personally built and launched a campaign in the last two years, this is not the right fit. 
 What You Will Own 
 Plan and forecast 
 Develop the annual and quarterly marketing plan tied to revenue targets: audiences, offers, campaign choices, investment and expected results, by practice. 
 Own marketing's qualified pipeline forecast with Sales and the RevOps lead: expected opportunities, conversion, timing and dependencies. 
 Review funnel performance weekly and recommend what to scale, change or stop. 
 Conference and buyer-event campaigns 
 Select conferences because the right buyers attend and a practice has a relevant offer. Set the commercial objective, target accounts, budget, meeting goal, seller commitments and follow-up plan. 
 Connect each conference to pre-event engagement, booked meetings with target accounts, an adjacent dinner, roundtable or expert session where it improves access, and disciplined post-event follow-up. 
 Decide, with evidence, whether to proceed, resize or stop an event. 
 Named-account campaigns 
 With sellers, select accounts, identify the buyer and a credible business problem, and choose the offer or evidence that fits. 
 Write the campaign brief and coordinate organic LinkedIn, email, website conversion paths and seller outreach against clear audiences, deliverables and commercial goals. 
 Review conversion from reach to meaningful response, held meeting, sales acceptance and opportunity, and adjust. 
 Funnel, HubSpot and Sales alignment 
 Define, with Sales, what counts as a marketing-qualified lead, what sales acceptance means, how fast handoffs happen and how sourced and influenced pipeline are recorded. Hold both sides to it. 
 Work with the RevOps lead on HubSpot segmentation, routing, campaign tracking and reporting. You can build in HubSpot yourself and you expect your team to. 
 Preserve the distinctions between marketing-sourced, partner-sourced and sales-sourced pipeline so the numbers stay credible. 
 Team and operating rhythm 
 Lead and coach the content and field marketing specialists; brief and prioritize design work; set expectations and give direct, useful feedback. 
 Run one campaign brief format, one shared calendar, a weekly delivery review, a weekly funnel review with Sales and a monthly spend and attribution review. 
 Coordinate with the Community & Media Lead so editorial, podcast and community programs and commercial campaigns reinforce each other, with a single owner for every deliverable. 
 Hands-on delivery 
 Personally produce campaign briefs, LinkedIn and email copy, landing-page requirements, HubSpot workflows, launch checks and performance reviews. 
 Use AI heavily for research, drafting, repurposing and analysis, with verification and accountability for what ships. 
What Success Looks Like 
 First 90 days 
 Days 1 to 30: assess offers, active campaigns, assets, the funnel and team capacity; validate the first two campaign priorities with the Chief Strategy Officer and Sales. 
 Days 31 to 60: launch one coordinated campaign; establish the shared calendar, seller commitments and HubSpot handoff checks. 
 Days 61 to 90: review cohort conversion and spend; improve the second campaign; recommend targets and capacity changes for the year. 
 Year one measures 
 Marketing-sourced qualified pipeline against the agreed target, with a forecast you can explain and defend. 
 100% of launched campaigns have an approved brief, a named seller owner, a budget, tracking and a follow-up plan. 
 At least 90% of agreed milestones delivered on time across the team. 
 Weekly review of conversion, spend, opportunity progression and overdue handoffs with Sales and the RevOps lead, with performance improving from the starting baseline. 
What You Bring  
 Typically six or more years of B2B marketing, including integrated campaigns you personally planned, built, launched and improved within the last two to three years. 
 Demonstrated organic demand generation in a complex B2B buying environment (long cycles, multiple stakeholders): conferences and buyer events, named-account or ABM campaigns, organic LinkedIn, email and website conversion. 
 Fluency in funnel math and attribution: MQL, sales acceptance, held meeting, qualified opportunity, pipeline and bookings. You know what you can prove and what you cannot, and you do not count everything as pipeline. 
 Hands-on CRM and marketing automation. HubSpot is preferred; practical Salesforce, Marketo or comparable experience is acceptable. 
 Experience leading or mentoring contributors while continuing to deliver briefs, copy, workflows and analysis yourself. 
 Strong writing, sound budget judgment and credibility with sellers, executives and subject-matter experts. 
 Practical, verified use of AI with evidence that it made your delivery faster or better. 
 Asset: experience marketing to supply chain, logistics, 3PL, or enterprise technology and services buyers. 
 Paid-advertising expertise is not required. Demonstrable ownership and execution matter more than any specific title.
 Why You'll Love Working Here 
 At Fulfillment IQ, we don't just build supply chain solutions; we build long-term careers. We operate with a high-trust, high-standards culture that values clear thinking, collaboration and accountability without unnecessary hierarchy. 
 Work That Matters: You will build the marketing engine for a company whose work changes how goods move for brands, retailers and 3PLs. Your campaigns put real experts in front of real buyers with real problems. 
 Ownership and Influence: A small team with direct access to the Chief Strategy Officer, practice leaders and sellers. Your decisions show up in the pipeline, not in a slide. 
 Career Growth: A dedicated learning and development budget, mentorship from experienced operators, and room to grow as the function grows. 
 Flexibility: Hybrid work from our Toronto / GTA office three days per week, with flexible hours around delivery and event needs. 
 Recognition: We celebrate team wins, anniversaries and milestones, and we are clear about who did the work. 
 Collaborative Culture: Colleagues who value direct communication, sound judgment and follow-through. 
Benefits  
 Extended health and dental coverage for you and your family 
 Competitive paid time off, sick leave and public holidays, with flexible leave policies 
 Group retirement savings plan with employer contributions 
 Dedicated learning and development budget 
 Equipment and workstation allowances, internet and business travel reimbursements 
 Team events, meetups and company offsites 
 Important Information for Applicants 
 Work Authorization 
 Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada.
 Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring:  
 FIQ uses artificial intelligence to assist in the screening, assessment, and shortlisting of applications for this position, including features within our applicant tracking system. AI supports human reviewers and does not make hiring decisions on its own. Final hiring decisions are made by FIQ personnel. If you have questions about how AI is used in this process, contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com. 
 Accommodations:  
 FIQ is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Consistent with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code, accommodations are available on request at any stage of recruitment and assessment. Contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com and we will work with you to meet your needs. 
 Candidate Privacy:  
 Your personal information is collected and used for recruitment purposes in accordance with FIQ's Candidate Privacy Notice, available  here , and in accordance with applicable Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA). This includes the use of AI-assisted screening described above and cross-border storage or processing that may occur in the United States. By applying, you acknowledge this notice. Questions: hr@fulfillmentiq.com. 
 Equal Opportunity:  
 Fulfillment IQ is a people-first company built on trust, collaboration, and ownership. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any ground protected under the Ontario Human Rights Code, including race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, or disability. 
 Learn More About Us: 
 Website:   fulfillmentiq.com 
 LinkedIn:   Fulfillment IQ 
 Spotify:   eCom Logistics Podcast Spotify 
 YouTube:   eCom Logistics Podcast YouTube

 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead.  Brand Studio builds and evolves the systems, experiences, and programs that shape how Stripe shows up in the world. We create high-quality, versatile, and forward-looking brand systems and help teams across Stripe use them clearly and consistently.
 What you’ll do

 In partnership with Brand producers and designers, you will identify gaps and opportunities in Stripe’s brand system, help the team enhance and evolve it, and translate decisions into clear rationale and guidance. Your portfolio will include Stripe’s brand consultation program, AI-enabled brand operations, the Identity team’s migration to a new digital asset management system, and the merchandise program.
 Responsibilities 
 Lead the Identity team’s workstream for Stripe’s new digital asset management (DAM) system, partnering with the Marketing teams to migrate and organize assets in a clear and usable way.
 Own and continuously improve Stripe’s brand consultation program, identifying recurring needs that can be addressed through clearer guidance, reusable templates, automation, or AI-enabled self-service.
 Help scale and evolve Stripe’s brand system in partnership with Brand Producers and designers, improving how guidance is documented, shared, and applied. 
 Partner with Brand Producers to develop a connected brand operating system and home base for Brand Studio’s internal AI tools; prototype workflows, evaluate their reliability, and support adoption across design teams and cross-functional partners.
 Lead a portfolio of brand systems and operations programs, including roadmap development, budgets, resourcing, project scoping, and timelines.
 Manage Stripe’s merchandise program operations, including budgets, invoices, vendor relationships, warehouse inventory, product testing and launches, and RFPs for new vendors.
 Partner with cross-functional design, marketing, technical, and operational teams to support the consistent application of Stripe’s brand across surfaces.
 Drive clarity through documentation, tooling, operating rhythms, and updates; connect teams, anticipate risks, and proactively resolve blockers.
 Uphold and advocate for design quality while helping creatives establish practices that make high-quality work easier to produce.

They have strong design sense and apply it to the operational decisions that protect quality, reduce friction, and keep programs moving.
 The ideal candidate excels at operating complex, evolving programs while maintaining and raising the bar on craft. They are curious and experimental with AI, offer thoughtful options and tradeoffs, articulate decisions clearly, and collaborate effectively with leadership, creatives, cross-functional partners, and vendors. Most importantly, they are meticulous about details.

 Think users first: understand their needs, find thoughtful solutions, and continuously improve how they access and use brand guidance, tools, assets, and services.

 Have experience managing program budgets, tracking spend, and anticipating costs to keep work within budget.

 Actively use AI tools in day-to-day work and have experience prototyping, building, or implementing AI-enabled workflows or systems that others can adopt.
 Have experience operating in an in-house brand or creative environment with shared cross-functional resources and a lean production bench.
 Bring strong information architecture and knowledge management skills, with experience organizing documentation, tools, assets, metadata, or sources of truth.
 Have experience managing vendors; experience with procurement, inventory, physical goods, or merchandise is helpful but not required.
 Have a strong track record of influencing outcomes and building alignment across teams.
 Are highly detail-oriented, can balance speed and quality, and communicate clearly in writing and conversation.
 Are passionate about Stripe's mission to grow the internet economy.
